examples.en: I saw the moving moment of the victory with my own eyes.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 십 년 만에 만난 장면이 정말 감격적이었어요.
examples.en: The scene where the two met after ten years was truly moving.
The two families were reunited in an emotional moment.
I didn't know it would be this moving.
It isn't overwhelmingly moving, but it's a warm story.

examples.ko: 졸업식 노래가 너무 감격적이어서 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: The graduation song was so moving that I cried.

explain: '감격적인 + 명사'로 많이 쓰지만 '감격적이다', '감격적으로'처럼도 써요. '감동적'은 이야기나 영화처럼 마음을 움직이는 것에 넓게 쓰고, '감격적'은 큰 기쁨이나 고마움으로 가슴이 벅찬 순간에 어울려요.
explain_en: It is often used as '감격적인 + noun', but it also appears as '감격적이다' and '감격적으로'. '감동적' is broad and fits anything that touches you, like a story or film, while '감격적' suits moments when you are overcome with joy or gratitude.

examples.en: Nights living alone can sometimes feel lonely.
He lived a solitary life.

examples.ko: 사람들 속에 있어도 고독할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Even among people there are times I feel alone.

examples.ko: 산 위에 서 있는 나무가 고독해 보였어요.
examples.en: The tree standing on the mountain looked lonely.
This song has a lonely and desolate mood.
The first year studying abroad was truly lonely.

explain: 고독하다는 곁에 사람이 없어서 느끼는 쓸쓸함, 또는 혼자라는 상태를 깊이 느끼는 감정이에요. '외롭다'는 일상에서 누구나 쓰는 말이고, 고독하다는 소설이나 노래 가사처럼 좀 더 무겁고 문학적인 느낌이에요. 친구에게 말할 때는 '외로워요'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Godokhada is the deep feeling of loneliness from having no one beside you, or from being alone. 외롭다 is the everyday word anyone uses, while 고독하다 feels heavier and more literary, like in novels and song lyrics. To a friend, 외로워요 sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 친구의 넋두리를 두 시간이나 들어 줬어요.
examples.en: I listened to my friend's grumbling for two whole hours.

examples.ko: 그는 신세 한탄 같은 넋두리를 계속 늘어놓아요.
examples.en: He keeps going on with self-pitying complaints.

examples.ko: 힘든 일이 있으면 저한테 넋두리라도 하세요.
examples.en: If something is hard, at least vent to me.
Grandmother's lament went on so long that the meal got cold.
This isn't a complaint, just me venting.

examples.ko: 넋두리만 하지 말고 해결 방법을 찾아봐요.
examples.en: Let's look for a solution instead of just grumbling.

explain: 보통 '넋두리를 하다/늘어놓다'로 써요. 신세나 억울한 일을 혼잣말처럼 길게 투덜대는 느낌이고, '푸념'과 비슷해요. 해결을 바라기보다 속상한 마음을 쏟아내는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is usually used as '넋두리를 하다/늘어놓다'. It feels like long, mumbling grumbling about your lot or something unfair, similar to '푸념'. It is about pouring out frustration rather than seeking a solution.

examples.en: Last night I had a truly sweet dream.
The newlyweds are still lost in sweet dreams.
The sweet dream of passing did not last long.
The sweet dream broke and reality began.
I woke from the sweet dream of the trip and went back to work.
The dreamlike time passed in an instant.

explain: 잠잘 때 꾸는 꿈보다 행복한 기대나 희망을 비유하는 말로 더 많이 써요. '단꿈을 꾸다', '단꿈에 젖다'처럼 말하고, 반대말은 '악몽'이에요.
explain_en: It is used more often as a metaphor for happy hopes and expectations than for an actual dream while sleeping. It appears as '단꿈을 꾸다' or '단꿈에 젖다', and the opposite is '악몽' (nightmare).

en: to contemplate; to think; to meditate

examples.ko: 저는 주말 아침에 공원을 걸으며 사색해요.
examples.en: On weekend mornings, I walk in the park and reflect.

examples.ko: 혼자 조용히 사색하고 싶어서 여행을 떠났어요.
examples.en: I went on a trip because I wanted to reflect quietly alone.

examples.ko: 그는 인생에 대해 오래 사색하는 사람이에요.
examples.en: He is someone who thinks deeply about life for a long time.

examples.ko: 사색할 시간이 없을 만큼 요즘 너무 바빠요.
examples.en: I'm so busy these days that I have no time to reflect.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 창가에 앉아 사색하곤 해요.
examples.en: On rainy days, I often sit by the window and contemplate.

examples.ko: 책을 읽다가 잠시 사색했더니 생각이 정리됐어요.
examples.en: After pausing to reflect while reading, my thoughts became clearer.

explain: '생각하다'보다 혼자 조용히, 깊이 생각을 이어 가는 느낌이 있어요. 명사 '사색'과 함께 '사색에 잠기다'라고도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Compared with '생각하다' (to think), it has a feel of quietly and deeply following your thoughts alone. Together with the noun '사색', you will also often hear '사색에 잠기다' (to be lost in thought).

en: to think about seriously; to contemplate

examples.en: I reflect on my day while writing in my diary.

examples.ko: 실수를 성찰하지 않으면 같은 일이 또 생겨요.
examples.en: If you don't reflect on your mistakes, the same thing will happen again.

examples.ko: 잠들기 전에 오늘 한 말을 조용히 성찰했어요.
examples.en: Before falling asleep, I quietly reflected on what I said today.
Sometimes you need time to reflect on yourself.

examples.ko: 선생님은 우리에게 지난 한 해를 성찰해 보라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher told us to reflect on the past year.
After reflecting on my fault, I apologized to my friend.

explain: '반성하다'는 잘못을 뉘우치는 느낌이 강하고, '성찰하다'는 잘못뿐 아니라 자신의 생각과 삶을 깊이 돌아볼 때 써요. 글, 수업, 면접에서 '자기 성찰'로 자주 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '돌아보다'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: '반성하다' strongly means repenting of a wrong, while '성찰하다' is used for looking deeply at your thoughts and life as a whole, not only your faults. It often appears as '자기 성찰' (self-reflection) in writing, classes and interviews, and in daily talk people often say '돌아보다'.

en: (one's mind) to take a new turn

examples.en: This new year I'll turn over a new leaf and start exercising.
I cut my hair short to make a fresh start.
We need to change the mood and refresh our spirit.
After coming back from vacation, I felt renewed.

examples.ko: 다 같이 심기일전하는 마음으로 다시 시작해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's all start over with a fresh mindset.

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어졌지만 심기일전하고 다시 공부하고 있어요.
examples.en: I failed the exam, but I've pulled myself together and am studying again.

explain: 안 좋은 일이 있은 뒤나 새 출발을 앞두고 마음가짐을 확 바꿀 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '마음을 다잡다', '새 마음으로'라고도 말해요. 새해, 휴가 뒤, 실패 뒤처럼 전환점에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used when you completely reset your attitude after something bad or before a new start. In everyday talk people also say '마음을 다잡다' or '새 마음으로'. It fits turning points such as a new year, after a vacation or after a failure.

examples.en: I tried asking and answering questions to myself alone in my room.
He prepared for the interview by asking and answering questions himself.
It was a speech where the speaker asked questions and answered them himself.
When you're worried, asking and answering yourself helps organize your thoughts.
When no one answered, he ended up answering his own question.
As I asked and answered myself, the answer became clear.

explain: 스스로 묻고 스스로 대답한다는 점에서 그냥 혼잣말을 하는 것과 달라요. 고민을 정리할 때도 쓰고, 발표나 글에서 질문을 던진 뒤 직접 답하는 방식을 가리키기도 해요.
explain_en: It differs from simple talking to yourself because you both ask and answer the question. It is used for sorting out worries, and also for presentations or writing where the speaker poses a question and then answers it directly.

en: to criticize; to comment; to review

examples.en: How do critics review that novel?

examples.ko: 선생님은 제 글을 솔직하게 평해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My teacher gave me an honest review of my writing.

examples.ko: 친구가 제 노래를 어떻게 평했는지 궁금해요.
examples.en: I wonder how my friend judged my singing.

examples.ko: 사람들이 그 식당을 맛있다고 평하는 이유를 알겠어요.
examples.en: I understand why people say that restaurant is delicious.

examples.ko: 남의 외모를 함부로 평하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't carelessly comment on other people's looks.

examples.ko: 전문가들은 이번 경기를 아주 훌륭했다고 평했어요.
examples.en: Experts said this match was excellent.

explain: 그냥 '말하다'가 아니라 좋고 나쁨을 따져서 말할 때 써요. 보통 '~라고 평하다' 꼴로 쓰고, 말보다 글이나 뉴스에서 더 많이 보여요. 대화에서는 '평가하다'나 '이야기하다'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '말하다' (to say), it means giving a judgment about good or bad points. It usually appears as '~라고 평하다' and is seen more in writing and news than in speech. In conversation, people also use '평가하다' or '이야기하다'.

examples.en: After the concert, he expressed thanks to the fans.
I'd like to show my respect to my teacher.

examples.ko: 많은 사람이 유감을 표하며 사과를 요구했어요.
examples.en: Many people expressed regret and demanded an apology.

examples.ko: 불만을 표하기 전에 먼저 상황을 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Before expressing dissatisfaction, check the situation first.

examples.ko: 반대를 표하는 사람은 손을 들어 주세요.
examples.en: Those who express opposition, please raise your hand.

examples.ko: 장례식장에서 조의를 표할 때는 조용히 인사해요.
examples.en: When you offer condolences at a funeral, you greet people quietly.

explain: '표현하다'와 비슷하지만 단독으로 쓰지 않고 '감사를 표하다, 유감을 표하다, 반대를 표하다'처럼 감정이나 태도를 나타내는 명사와 함께 써요. 뉴스나 인사말처럼 격식 있는 말투에서 잘 나와요.
explain_en: It is similar to '표현하다' but is not used alone; it pairs with nouns of feeling or attitude, as in '감사를 표하다', '유감을 표하다' and '반대를 표하다'. It fits formal speech such as news and greetings.
